title: I want to make animations of my characters, what is the current best AI for doing this task?
author: ElectricStrawbeary
selftext:
So I am currently working on an animation of a character posing, but so far I have been using Chatgpt Codex, using the Dots and also have had the 100$ version of the membership paid off, and yet it is still providing me with very crudely made animations

I even have the MCP linked directly from blender into Chatgpt and yet it still does a rather luke warm execution every time

Is there an ai that has been performing specifically 3D model animation better than the rest?

replies.author: FrozenFirebat
replies.body: Unimate is for educational purposes, they don't own the data, so if you ever want to be commercial with your product, you open yourself to liability.

replies.body:
What he shared has MIT licence.  
[https://github.com/Friedrich-M/UniMate/blob/main/LICENSEIDK](https://github.com/Friedrich-M/UniMate/blob/main/LICENSEIDK)   
IDK what you are referring to on educational license? I searched other sources too and could not find it.

replies.author: FrozenFirebat
replies.body: Mixamo, for example is proprietary, and their own license gives you the right to use the animations in limited capacity (it's wide, but not unlimited). While the Unimate license says that you can use it for whatever you want, it's existence technically breaks Adobe's license and using it, you inherit that.

replies.body:

I get wat you are saying now. Issue you see is that that Unimate used data to train sourced from Adobe Mixamo. The Mixamo license.

Did not know much about how unimate was trained until I looked it up after being confused why adobe was brought up haha.

comments.author: DigitalDustChan
comments.body: The problem is that when you break character animation down to math it just doesn't work very well. Natural movement uses a lot of messy curves that don't look good in data but look good on the screen. Your best bet is to find an animation library. Any good animation library is generated using motion capture. Take that library and either use something from it directly or get the AI to blend some of the animations from that.

comments.author: redditscraperbot2
comments.body:
I'd propose you use H3 or your video generator of choice to create motion capture footage and then use unreal's metahuman motion capture to animation and clean with an AI. It can do a much better job of cleaning, adding weight to frames and fixing penetration than it can building from scratch.

\>but I don't use metahumans

no problem, you can retarget it in blender to the rig of your choice. It's trivial for an LLM.

That's the best free mocap choice in my opinion. You can also use tools like kimodo to give you text to motion outputs, they will also need retargeting. I find they look a little janky if you stare at them long enough. They also don't animate the figures. Another thing that begins to stand out after a while.

comments.author: FrozenFirebat
comments.body: I've got some results from using seedance to make a video of my model doing an animation. That alone doesn't get you an animation, but you can use keyframes from the video and have AI match up poses on the model to the screenshots. Works even better if you can get Seedance to produce a video that shows the scene from multiple angles.

replies.author: Afraid-Fly-7030
replies.body: You can also feed these into metahuman animator or some other tool to get some 3d animation then either clean it up or use as reference.

comments.author: Cristazio
comments.body: Afaik the bast way to make sure you have good animations is to either use Mixamo or use mocap tools. There's also Cascadeur3D which IIRC can do text to animation, but I'm not 100% sure. ChatGPT and Claude can animate via code but i's not great. One thing you could try is giving ChatGPT the poses the character has to perform via images and tell it to connect them together, the result may not be ideal but it beata having to go and get a new subscription just for that.
